old: (“history will be kind to me, for I intend to write it”)
new: (he told Parliament in 1948 that he proposed “to write that history myself”; the popular line “history will be kind to me, for I intend to write it” is a misquotation)
problem: The famous line is a misquotation; Churchill’s documented 1948 Commons remark was that he proposed “to write that history myself”.

old: and quickly backed the 1973 junta, though declassified files show no direct US role in the coup itself and Pakistan during the 1971 Bangladesh genocide;
new: and quickly backed the 1973 junta, though declassified files have not shown a direct US role in the coup itself; backed Pakistan during the 1971 Bangladesh genocide;
problem: Garbled sentence makes it read as if files show no US role regarding Pakistan; Nixon and Kissinger backed Pakistan in 1971 (Bass, The Blood Telegram), and ‘show no role’ overstates what the records prove.
sources: Gary J. Bass, The Blood Telegram (2013)

new: Edwin Moise now estimates on the rough order of 10,000
problem: Moise’s own published revision puts executions at ‘perhaps on the rough order of 10,000’ (up from about 5,000), not 15,000.

new: abdication announced November 9, 1918 (he formally signed it on November 28);
problem: Prince Max von Baden announced the abdication on November 9 without Wilhelm’s consent; Wilhelm signed his formal abdication on November 28, 1918.
sources: John Röhl, Wilhelm II: Into the Abyss of War and Exile (2014)

old: The postwar claim that the bombs saved “a million” American lives comes mainly from a 1947 article by former War Secretary Henry Stimson written to answer critics; 1945 planning estimates varied widely, from tens of thousands to several hundred thousand casualties.
new: The postwar claim that the bombs saved “a million” American lives comes mainly from a 1947 article by former War Secretary Henry Stimson written to answer critics (he actually wrote of “over a million casualties”, which counts the wounded); 1945 estimates varied widely, from tens of thousands of casualties in some military plans to over a million in others (a study for Stimson’s staff projected 1.7–4 million).
problem: Stimson wrote ‘casualties’, not lives, and 1945 estimates were not capped at several hundred thousand: the Joint Chiefs’ April 1945 figure for both invasions was about 1.2 million casualties and the Shockley memo projected 1.7–4 million.
sources: D. M. Giangreco, Hell to Pay (2009); summarized at https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Downfall#Estimated_casualties

old: US diplomats handed over lists of communist names (US cables declassified in 2017)
new: US diplomats handed over lists of communist names (first reported in 1990), and US embassy cables declassified in 2017 show officials followed the killings in detail
problem: The name lists were revealed by Kathy Kadane’s 1990 reporting, not by the 2017 cable release, which documented US officials’ detailed knowledge of the killings.

old: helped by about $11 billion of US and British Lend-Lease supplies
new: helped by about $11 billion of US Lend-Lease supplies plus British aid
problem: The roughly $11.3 billion figure is US Lend-Lease to the USSR alone; British aid was additional.
Sukarno had a single name; ‘Ahmed/Achmed’ was a foreign press invention (the file elsewhere uses ‘Sukarno’).
